version_history.note: Namespaces and codes as approved in plan v1.2.1 section 8.3. Codes only; no transition graph.

Wave 5 stream 3. Adds initial_status, the explicit transition graph, the writer registry and the badge precedence. The codes are UNCHANGED - this version makes the registry executable rather than descriptive, so that an unreachable state fails the build instead of sitting in the file forever.

rule: Integration and job statuses are OPERATIONAL. They are visible to administrators on SCR-26, SCR-38 and SCR-39. They must NEVER be rendered on a business screen as if they were C3 business statuses. A contract test enforces this.
relationship_to_C3: Disjoint, with one deliberate exception: C3 contains INTEGRATION_FAILED and RECONCILIATION_PENDING, which are the two business-visible consequences of integration state. Those two C3 codes are the ONLY sanctioned bridge from this namespace to a business screen.

business_visible_bridge.note: Objects carry a separate integration_state badge alongside their C3 business status, rather than adding a 22nd business status. This is precisely why the registries are separated.

derivation.QUEUED: an integration_outbox row exists for this object in state PENDING
derivation.SENT: outbox row in state SENT and external_id populated
derivation.FAILED: outbox row in state FAILED or DEAD -> also sets C3 business status INTEGRATION_FAILED

business_visible_bridge.precedence_reason: An object may carry several outbox rows - a PO emission and a later amendment. A single badge must be deterministic. FAILED outranks QUEUED outranks SENT, so the badge never reports success while an emission for the same object is broken. Without an ordering the badge would depend on row order, which is the kind of defect that only shows up in production.
business_visible_bridge.no_outbox_row: no badge at all - NOT a fourth badge value, and never SENT. An object that was never queued has no integration state to report.
business_visible_bridge.hard_rule: The badge is rendered in its own slot with its own label. It is NEVER substituted for, merged into, or rendered by the C3 status pill component. That substitution is the specific defect these separated registries exist to prevent.

writers.note: The single module that may COMPUTE a transition is app/backend/integration/statuses.py (stream 3). The modules below are the only callers permitted to PERSIST the resulting state. Recorded here so that a state with no writer is visible as a defect rather than as an omission.

operator.file: app/backend/api/ - SCR-27 and SCR-39 manual actions

statuses.meaning: Could not be attributed or mapped. Raised a reconciliation_exception. NEVER guessed, never spread pro-rata, never dropped.
Duplicate payload_sha for an already-processed external_id. Idempotent no-op.
Exceeded max_attempts. Visible on SCR-39 with manual retry.

transitions.side_effect: reconciliation_exception kind UNMAPPED_EXTERNAL_STATUS; external_status_raw preserved verbatim

transitions.note: An operator resolves the exception on SCR-27 by supplying the missing attribution or the missing mapping row. The payload is then applied - it is never applied on a guess.

statuses.meaning: Enqueued inside the business transaction. Not yet sent.
Retryable failure. next_attempt_at set with exponential backoff and full jitter.

transitions.note: Enqueued in the SAME transaction as the business write. There is no window in which the business fact is committed and the emission is not.

Zoho documents no idempotency header (plan section 11.6). A send killed after despatch but before recording is recovered by looking the document up on the unique custom field cf_capex_ref and UPDATING it. A dedupe hit is a SUCCESS - not a duplicate, and not a failure.

transitions.side_effect: object business status set to C3 INTEGRATION_FAILED

transitions.note: A 4xx business error is not retried - see rate_limit_classification.4xx_business_error.
transitions.side_effect: reconciliation_exception; object business status set to C3 INTEGRATION_FAILED

job.description: One bounded, chunked, checkpointed background job. Ceiling 15 minutes on Catalyst Cron/Event Functions; soft deadline 12 minutes.

statuses.meaning: Claimed via SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED. locked_until set for crash reaping.
Soft deadline reached; progress committed and a resumable cursor persisted. Resumes on the next tick.
Exceeded max_attempts or max_resume_count. Alerts rather than looping forever.

transitions.note: 12 minutes against the 15-minute Catalyst ceiling. Progress is COMMITTED before the state moves.
Crash reaping. locked_until has passed, so the claim is void and the job is re-claimable.
A job that checkpoints forever is not making progress. resume_count is bounded so that it alerts instead of consuming the daily call ceiling in silence.

statuses.meaning: 5 consecutive counted failures in 60s, or daily quota exhausted. No calls attempted until next_probe_at.
A single probe call is permitted. Success closes; failure reopens.

transitions.note: On ERP Standard the DAILY ceiling is the binding one, not the per-minute. next_probe_at is the next day boundary.

circuit.naming_note: Prefixed CIRCUIT_ deliberately. The bare code CLOSED collides with the C3 business status CLOSED, and the two mean opposite things - a closed circuit is healthy and passing traffic, whereas a closed project is terminal and blocks posting. The collision was caught by tests/test_contracts.py::test_integration_statuses_are_disjoint_from_business_statuses on first run.

rate_limit_classification.note: Zoho error codes are handled distinctly. Only genuine vendor failures count toward the circuit breaker.

429_code_44_per_minute.reason: our own throttle failed, not the vendor

429_code_45_daily_quota.action: open circuit until next day boundary, alert

429_code_1070_concurrency.action: reduce parallelism by 1, retry with jitter

401_invalid_token.action: refresh once; second failure opens circuit and raises P1

4xx_business_error.action: no retry; QUARANTINED or DEAD plus a reconciliation_exception
